text:
Lina: Heads-up — Acme Legal asked for a temporary routing override so their traffic goes to their Dedicated pool while they finish validation. They want ad-hoc allowlist entries we can toggle from the console.
Sandeep: Can they do that via header or do we need a tenant-level flag?
Lina: They asked for a header because their proxy team can inject it: `X-Redwood-Route: dedicated=acme-v2;reason=contract;ttl=3600`
Max: 🙀 headers are tricky — we strip most org headers at the edge for security. If we allow this, we need HMAC or signed token, TTL, and an approver audit entry.
Priya: Agree. Also need to ensure this doesn't bypass quotas or cost controls. Dedicated remains billable to the org, but we must not let a header route to dedicated if the org isn't on the dedicated plan.
Marta: From PM side, console UX should show: who created override, TTL, justification, approver, and a kill-switch. Also surface telemetry: override-uses, tokens rejected, per-hour reroutes.
Lina: Proposed quick spec: 1) API: POST /orgs/:id/overrides {target: "dedicated:acme-v2", ttl: 3600, reason: "legal-testing"} returns an opaque token; 2) Edge verifies token signature and expiry; 3) Console lists active overrides and audit trail.
Sandeep: Example token header we could accept (short):
```
X-Redwood-Override: eyJhbGci...signed...;org=acme123;exp=1716435700
```
Max: Runtime checks: edge should check org entitlement, check token sig with KMS, and attach `x-routing-reason` to request metadata for telemetry. If any check fails, fall back to normal routing and log at WARN.
Priya: Telemetry ask: add metrics `routing.override.applied`, `routing.override.denied`, and tag by `org_id` and `target_pool`. Hook into the console graphing so support can see spike of overrides.
analytics-bot: metric `routing.override.applied` created in staging (sample rate 1.0)
Lina: One operational question — do we allow console-created overrides without token (i.e., admin click creates server-side binding)? That would be simpler for enterprise admins.
Max: Yes, server-side binding is fine for console-created entries. But header-supplied tokens must be signed and single-use or TTL-limited. For audit we should store: creator_id, method (console|token), ip, and revoke_ts.
Marta: UX note — show TTL countdown and a reason field (free text + optional template). Make revoke a two-click action with a warning.
Priya: Also add policy: console overrides can't exceed 7 days without legal-approved extension. Short TTL by default (1 hour) for token-based.
Lina: I'll write a tiny PR for the API shape and add a draft to the console mockups. tagging @Sandeep @Max for security/runtime items.
Sandeep: Sounds good — I'll scope the KMS signing + verification and drop a design doc link here when ready. :thumbsup:
Max: I'll add the runtime checks and telemetry tags. Quick ops command to find current uses: `rg "override.*acme123" /var/log/redwood/routing/*.log | tail -n 200`
Priya: Filing a small infra request to ensure quota enforcement layer checks `is_override_allowed(org)` before routing — I'll ping infra.
devops-bot: deploy queued: routing-edge/verify-token v0.3 -> staging at 1716432500
Lina: Nice. If we can land this in staging today we can demo to Acme tomorrow. Thanks team. :rocket:
